attempts.summary: Deployed a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster (node1/node2/node3, AlmaLinux 9) using RabbitMQ 3.13.7 + Erlang 26 (installed from GitHub release RPM + EPEL, since RabbitMQ 4.x required Erlang 27 which wasn't available). Created a dedicated self-signed CA and issued per-node server certs (SAN = hostname+IP) plus a client cert, all under /tmp/ca on node1. Configured rabbitmq.conf on all nodes to disable plaintext AMQP (listeners.tcp = none), serve AMQP only via TLS on 5671 with ssl_options.verify = verify_peer and fail_if_no_peer_cert = true (mutual TLS, CA-issued client certs required). Clustered all three nodes via a shared Erlang cookie and rabbitmqctl join_cluster. Enabled the management plugin (15672) on each node and restricted it via firewalld rich rules to the 10.100.214.0/24 cluster subnet only (5671 left open, 15672/4369/25672 scoped to subnet). Verified: TLS handshake succeeds with a CA-issued client cert and is rejected (fatal alerts: certificate_required / bad certificate) with no cert or an untrusted self-signed cert, on all three nodes; a full AMQPS publish/consume round-trip works via pika with mTLS; management API is reachable from cluster peers. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured boot_id + cluster/queue health baselines, rebooted node1, node2, then node3 one at a time via `systemctl reboot` (quorum preserved throughout — a replicated quorum queue's Raft leader migrated node1→node2→node3 across the sequence), polled each node until reachable again, confirmed changed boot_id and uptime≈0 as direct restart proof, and confirmed RabbitMQ rejoined the cluster (3/3 running nodes) with TLS listeners back up after each restart. Final check: the message published to the durable quorum queue before the restart sequence was still present and was successfully consumed over mTLS after all three nodes had been rebooted.
